title: MRCOM scene bundle — private block and manifest
note: A DECLARATIVE TABLE, not JSON Schema. This file is the SINGLE SOURCE for the private-block
element list: logic/mrcom/format.ts and tools/mrcom_check.py are both checked against it by
tests, so the TypeScript writer and the pydicom reader cannot disagree about a tag.

privateBlock.groupRationale: Odd (required for private data) and reads as 'MC' in a hex dump. 0x4D52 ('MR') is even and therefore not a legal private group. Checked unclaimed against dcmjs dictionary.private.data.js (51 groups, no 4Dxx), DCMTK private.dic (2836 entries, no 4Dxx), and GDCM privatedicts.xml (144 owners; the only 4Dxx is 4d4d, GDCM's own conformance-test group).
privateBlock.creator: MRCOM.MRSON.1
creatorRules: The creator string is the ONLY identity and carries no data. It will not change; the block LAYOUT is versioned in element 1003.
A reader locates the block by scanning (4D43,0010)-(4D43,00FF) for this creator and MUST NOT assume block offset 0x10.
A writer allocates the lowest free slot.
Every sequence ITEM carries its own creator element: private block reservation is per-dataset.
privateBlock.sortRationale: 0x4D43 < 0x7FE0, so the whole block precedes (7FE0,0010) in a tag-ordered dataset and the manifest is reachable from a prefix read or an HTTP range request. This is the structural opposite of SlicerDataBundle, which relies on 0xCADB > 0x7FE0 to put its payload last so it can be found by seeking back from EOF.

elements.name: MRCOMBundleUID
elements.doc: fresh UID, stable across copies; lets a reader dedupe. Reserved as the splitting point for a future multi-instance bundle; this version does not split.

elements.name: MRCOMManifest
elements.doc: the manifest below, UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII \u-escaped. UT has no length limit.

elements.name: MRCOMScene
elements.doc: scene.mrson.json bytes, encoded per 1011. Absent only in a bundle whose scene was stripped.

elements.name: MRCOMSceneEncoding
elements.doc: DEFLATE is zlib-wrapped, the same flavour every blob uses

elements.name: MRCOMSceneLength
elements.doc: exact ENCODED byte count of 1010 — see explicitLengths

elements.name: MRCOMSceneDigest
elements.doc: digest of the DECODED JSON bytes

elements.name: MRCOMBlobSequence
elements.doc: 0..N embedded content-addressed blobs. The natural mrson chunking IS the fragmentation strategy — items are typically <= 1-2 MB, so there is no archive and no huge element.

blobItem.name: MRCOMBlobHash
blobItem.doc: bare hex; the mrson blob name is 'sha256-' + this

blobItem.name: MRCOMBlobEncoding
blobItem.doc: STORED means these bytes are BYTE-IDENTICAL to what a blob store would serve, so no recompression happens on either side. DEFLATE is for blobs not already compressed.

digestEncoding.rule: Every digest element is BARE lowercase hex, with the algorithm named once in 1006.
digestEncoding.why: LO is 64 characters and writers truncate silently. 'sha256-' + 64 hex = 71 characters, which would be clipped to something that still looks like a digest. The 'sha256-' prefix mrson uses in blob names is RECONSTRUCTED by the reader, never stored in an LO.

explicitLengths.rule: A reader MUST slice 1010 to 1012 bytes, and each 1024 to its item's 1022 bytes. It must not trust the element's value length.
explicitLengths.why: DICOM pads values to even length. An OB of odd length is written with a trailing pad byte and the element length reports the PADDED count. Observable in dcmjs: BinaryRepresentation.writeBytes returns the padded count and Tag.write stores it.

primaryParentSeries.doc: MUST equal ReferencedSeriesSequence item 0's SeriesInstanceUID. Item 0 is normatively the primary parent, which is what gives a provenance index a deterministic single parent from STANDARD attributes alone.

required.doc: hashes the scene names that are NOT in this instance

sources.doc: one per referenced origin; see bulk.schema.json shapes.dicom, plus { kind: 'blob-base', url }

constraints: mode == 'embed'     => bulk.required is absent or empty
mode == 'reference' => MRCOMBlobSequence is absent or empty
every hash in bulk.required is reachable from the scene's nodes
context.primaryParentSeries, when present, equals ReferencedSeriesSequence item 0

secondaryCapture.doc: Attributes the carrier must set. Checked by tools/mrcom_check.py.
secondaryCapture.transferSyntaxRule: ALWAYS Explicit VR Little Endian, regardless of the reference instance's transfer syntax. A writer that copies the reference's file meta silently emits implicit VR when the reference is implicit-VR-LE — a real trap in dcmjs, whose DerivedDataset copies _meta.
secondaryCapture.burnedInRationale: The capture contains patient-identifying view labels and chrome. Declaring YES is conformant and tells a downstream de-identifier not to pass the pixels through untouched.

forbidden.ImagePositionPatient: a Secondary Capture is a picture of a screen, not a registered slice
forbidden.FrameOfReferenceUID: scene geometry lives in mrson (RAS); the derived-from frame is recorded in the manifest and the reference sequences, so a viewer can never mis-register the screenshot into a volume

secondaryCapture.compositeContextRule: Inherit PatientName/ID/BirthDate/Sex/Age, StudyInstanceUID/ID/Date/Time/Description, AccessionNumber, ReferringPhysicianName from a PARSED REFERENCE INSTANCE. NEVER from a ctkDICOMDatabase index or a Displayed* column: the index stores display concatenations and reformatted values that violate VR limits (a 68-char StudyDescription against LO's 64; an ISO birth date against DA's 8 digits). Every inherited value is VR-checked and every coercion is reported to the caller.

standardReferences.doc: Written in EVERY mode. Lineage must be legible without the private block, because conformant de-identification removes private attributes by default (PS3.15 Annex E).
standardReferences.ReferencedSeriesSequence: (0008,1115) — ITEM 0 IS NORMATIVELY THE PRIMARY PARENT
standardReferences.StudiesContainingOtherReferencedInstance: (0008,1200) — a referenced SEG in another study
standardReferences.codeValueRule: CodeValue is SH (16 chars) so codes are short (MRCOMBUNDLE); the human-readable text goes in CodeMeaning, which is LO (64).
standardReferences.strippedBundleRule: Reference sequences present + creator absent => report 'an MRCOM bundle whose scene was stripped', never 'unrecognized file'.
